core_message: One volcano in Indonesia cooled the whole planet in 1815, causing a year without a summer, mass famine, and even Frankenstein.
title: The Volcano That Cancelled Summer
description:
Mount Tambora on Sumbawa, Indonesia, erupted in April 1815, with its climax on 10 April. It was a VEI-7 eruption, the most powerful in recorded history. Explosions were heard at least 2,600 km away, and the peak lost about a third of its height, dropping from about 4,300 m to 2,851 m. Around 10,000-11,000 people died from the eruption itself, and tens of thousands more from famine and disease; one estimate puts the total at at least 71,000.

Sulfur from the eruption cooled the climate. 1816 became the Year Without a Summer: global temperatures fell by about 0.4-0.7 degrees C, snow fell in Albany, New York, on 6 June, and crops failed across North America and Europe. That cold, wet summer, at the Villa Diodati by Lake Geneva, 18-year-old Mary Shelley began the story that became Frankenstein.

Source: Wikipedia, 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora.

comment_question: Would you survive a year without summer?

scenes.narration: In April 1815, a volcano in Indonesia exploded so violently that people heard it more than two and a half thousand kilometres away.
Mount Tambora lost about a third of its height. It was the most powerful eruption in recorded history, and around ten thousand people died in the eruption itself.
Its sulphur spread around the planet like a veil, dimming the sun. The next year, 1816, became known as the Year Without a Summer.
Snow fell in New York in June. Crops failed across Europe and North America, and famine followed. By one estimate, at least seventy thousand people died in all.
And in a rainy villa by a Swiss lake that cold summer, an eighteen year old named Mary Shelley began writing the story that became Frankenstein.
